definition: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning, an approach where agents reflect on past failures to improve their subsequent actions without updating model weights.
details: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning, an approach where agents reflect on past failures to improve their subsequent actions without updating model weights.

explainer.lead: An approach where language agents reflect on past failures to improve subsequent actions without updating model weights. It matters because it improves behavior through verbal feedback rather than retraining.

tiers.eli5: Like keeping a short diary of what went wrong last time and reading it before your next attempt, instead of having to relearn everything.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to let agents learn from failed attempts within the same model; the pitfall is that lessons live in text, not weights, so they must be carried into later attempts to have effect.
tiers.paperLevel: Described as Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning: agents reflect on past failures to improve their subsequent actions without updating model weights.

explainer.example: An agent fails a task, writes a note on what went wrong, and uses that note to adjust its next attempt — with no weight updates.
